name: Making bullets ricochet
goal: Several tanks in the game have special abilities. Most tanks however, share one similarity: their bullets 'bounce' x times off walls. The bounce count can differentiate per tank type, but the bounce logic remains the same. I need to create a script which makes the bullet ricochet.

approach.text:
There are several parts of code that need to be created for the ricochet to work. 
1. Detection: The bullet needs to detect that it collided with a wall. 
2. Calculating the reflected forward: If the bullet has 'bounces' left, the new direction needs to be calculated.
3. Rotating and setting the velocity.

To detect the walls, I had to use OnTriggerEnter or OnColliderEnter. From the source <<source Coppens, G. (2022, January 6). ‘OnCollisionEnter vs OnTriggerEnter ‘ when to use them? Medium. https://medium.com/nerd-for-tech/oncollisionenter-vs-ontriggerenter-when-to-use-them-37b08f3249a5#:~:text=OnCollisionEnter()%20is%20often%20used,to%20detect%20and%20interact%20with.>>, I learned that OnCollisionEnter is used for physics, whereas OnTriggerEnter is not.

The methods are invoked under different circumstances too. Letting physics be calculated by Unity caused the bullets to ricochet, but rotate continuously. Therefore, I had to calculate physics myself, and use the OnTriggerEnter method.

First I filtered out the entity collisions, like other bullets, tanks, and mines. If it was a wall, I just added a 90 degree rotation, as I tested it under a 45 degree angle. Using the source Add 90 Degrees to Transform.Rotation - Unity Answers. (19-11-2011). https: //answers.unity.com/questions/187506/add-90-degrees-to-transformrotation.html>> I found out it didn't work in all cases.

The following diagrams explain why it didn't work:
<<image 4.png>>
In the picture above the solution would work.
<<image 5.png>>
Here the solution does NOT work. Adding a 90* rotation results in the red direction. The correct direction, in green, rotates the bullet 45 degrees more. The problem gets more complicated if the bullet hits the walls from a different side, shown below:
<<image 6.png>>
The normals of the point where the bullet hits the wall, decides where the bullet deflects to, shown in orange in the diagram below:
<<image 7.png>>
By getting the rotation between the original direction and the normal (retrieved from a raycast), and adding it to the 'other side' of the normal, it produces the reflected direction. At this point, I thought other developers would have experienced the same problem, where they need to reflect something. I discovered that the Vector3 class had a static Reflect method that returns the new direction. With the new forward direction, it was easy to set the rotation and velocity of the bullet.

normalLearnings: I learned the difference and different use cases for OnTriggerEnter and OnCollisionEnter.
I learned that problems may share similarities that have already been solved by other people, or Unity itself in this case.
I learned how to calculate reflection myself.
I learned how to use Debug.DrawRay for debugging.
I learned I need to visualize different use cases before attempting to solve the first one I find.
